+Rakib Hasan No, you're absolutely wrong. That logic isn't applicable to the x60 series of NVIDIA graphics cards, and I can prove why:

The GTX 980 was the fastest single GPU NVIDIA had to offer at the time of its release/ The GTX 1080 is the fastest single GPU NVIDIA has to offer at the moment.

The GTX 970 was just as fast, if not faster, as the GTX 780 Ti/ GTX Titan Black - NVIDIA's flagship GPUs before the release of the Maxwell architecture/ The GTX 1070 is just as fast, if not faster, as the GTX 980 Ti/ GTX Titan X - NVIDIA's flagship GPUs before the release of the Pascal architecture.

The GTX 960 was, at its best, just as fast as a GTX 770. It will probably have much better power efficiency than the RX 480 as well.

P.S. One thing a lot of people tend to forget is that a big advantage AMD has over NVIDIA (for those who're on a budget, which is most likely the case if you're aiming for an RX 480) is FreeSync. Yes, I know NVIDIA has G-SYNC, but G-SYNC panels are generally much more expensive than FreeSync ones, despite offering generally similar features.
